analysis.title: GS MarketStrats | A Flush, Not Yet a Clearing
key_insights: Friday 11/20 looks like a classic positioning flush, but whether it was the clearing event is still open. S&P closed Friday at its lowest since April on heavy volume and poor breadth, then rallied 4.7% Monday led by Nvidia up 31.5%.

Credit stopped deteriorating but lagged the equity rebound. CDX IG and HY hit widest closes since late March Friday, and CDX recovered only about a quarter to a third of its widening versus roughly half of the equity fall.
CDX HY at 376bp is only 9bp inside Friday's 385bp. Credit catching up is the next confirmation the author wants.
Rates behaved better. The pressure partly came from higher real yields, which then fell. Monday's equity rally barely moved 10y nominal or real yields, and real yields remain above early-Nov levels.

The dollar is the awkward signal. DXY closed at 104.34, its highest since March 2025, partly on European pressure (colder weather, higher gas prices, wider US-Europe rate differentials), so it is not decisive alone.

EM is mixed. Last week local rates split by beta (PLN and KRW rallied, BRL and ZAR sold off) and eight of nine major EM currencies weakened. Monday brought a broad local curve rally but only a split EMFX recovery.
A clearing does not need fundamentals resolved. The AI capex and free-cash-flow debate persists and lower-quality credit remains stressed, but forced selling must have largely run its course.
Conditions for a clearing: Friday's S&P close holds, breadth stays reasonable without Nvidia up 30%, credit tightens, real yields stay below the Nov peak, and the dollar stops making highs.

Key line in the sand is CDX HY closing back above 385bp, which would make the author materially more cautious. Otherwise needs two of: S&P close below 6,910, 10y real yields above about 2.91%, DXY above 104.34 with renewed EMFX weakness.
If none trigger by end of next week, after a full post-Thanksgiving week, the author would be more comfortable treating Friday as the clearing.
